review.task_fit: no: a personal consumer in-car assistant for individual drivers, not a day-to-day city tool; the only municipal touchpoint is street-name narration built on GUGiK data, and no city feed, city-staff role or city-level decision is served.

scores.why: The voice-to-real-actions insight and the street-history narration over GUGiK PRG, TERYT, OSM and Wikipedia are genuinely thoughtful, but the core concept converges with CarPlay and Siri and the differentiating AI layer is unproven. Member C's 3 underrates it; the evidence supports the middle view shared by A and B.

Two of three members score 2 and the evidence backs them: navigation, parking and fuel come from Apple Maps search, and the one real urban data call feeds street trivia rather than city operations. Even A's own notes concede a single municipal touchpoint, so A's 5 is the unsupported outlier.

There is a clear user and a genuinely useful one-screen driving scenario with safety-minded details, but nothing verifies it runs: demo checks are empty, the team admits the AI is incomplete, and it requires an iOS 27 physical iPhone.

Eighteen screenshots and a 20-slide deck show a distinctive, consistent liquid-glass cockpit, though the running-app shots reveal placeholder map data, so the built UI trails the concept. C's 5 is the outlier against A and B.

About 13.5k lines of real Swift across 26 services with live MapKit routing, GUGiK and Polish speech integrations, but zero tests and no runtime evidence. A and B's reading matches the measured codebase; C's 3 rests on an unproven suspicion of undisclosed AI-generated code.

review.live_demo: none found in the form or README
review.built_during_event: partly: 1 commit before the event; 9 commits by 1 author, 2026-10-03 08:59 to 2026-10-04 08:02 UTC
strengths: Substantial real code, about 13.5k Swift lines across 26 services: MapKit routing with turn-by-turn guidance, a Polish speech pipeline with wake-word training, and camera capture.
Genuine open urban-data integration in PolishStreetKnowledgeService: GUGiK PRG OGC API, TERYT codes, Nominatim OSM and Wikipedia.
A distinctive, consistent liquid-glass landscape design carried across 18 screenshots and a 20-slide deck.
Safety-first UX discipline: overspeed voice warnings, music ducking, and honest refusals instead of invented answers.
weaknesses: It is a consumer driver app, not a Smart City tool: no city feed, no city-staff user, and the only municipal data is used for street narration.
No runtime proof of the core promise: demo checks are empty, there is no video, and there are zero test files and zero test cases.
The required presentation was not provided with the submission; the deck exists only inside the repo.
The team admits the AI functions are incomplete, and the AI path depends on specific hardware such as an iOS 27 physical iPhone and Apple Intelligence.
red_flags: May not be built for this task: a personal consumer in-car assistant for individual drivers, not a day-to-day city tool; the only municipal touchpoint is street-name narration built on GUGiK data, and no city feed, city-staff role or city-level decision is served.
The submission itself declares 'Not a finalist' and admits the AI functions are not fully complete, so the headline voice-AI claims go beyond what the evidence or the team's own statements support.
review.verdict: A seriously built and well-designed Polish in-car assistant with real code and real urban-data touches, but as submitted it is a personal consumer driving app rather than a Smart City tool, its core voice-AI promise is unverifiable from the evidence, and the required presentation was not delivered with the entry.
